title: The Ant and the Lazy Grasshopper
summary: A classic fable about a hardworking ant who stores food all summer and a carefree grasshopper who learns the value of preparation and kindness.
poll: Someone who refuses to prepare for the future does not deserve help later on.

versions.title: The Ant and the Lazy Grasshopper
versions.text:
An ant and a grasshopper lived in one field. All summer, the ant worked. She stored food for winter.

The grasshopper did not work. He played all day. He sang in the sun.

"Why work so hard?" he asked. "Come play!"

"I store food for winter," said the ant. "You should store food, too."

The grasshopper laughed. "Winter is far," he said. He kept playing.

At last, winter came. It was cold. Snow fell. The grasshopper had no food.

He was cold and hungry. He went to the ant's home.

"Please help me," he said. "I have no food."

The ant looked at him. She thought. Then she shared her food.

"Next year, you must prepare," she said. The grasshopper said yes. He learned to work and plan.

The grasshopper only laughed loudly at her warning. "Winter is still so far away," he said carelessly, and he kept playing happily all summer.

At last, winter finally arrived, and the weather turned bitterly cold. Snow covered the field, and the grasshopper suddenly had no food left anywhere.

Hungry and cold, he went to the ant's home and knocked on her door. "Please help me," he begged. "I have no food."

The ant looked at him for a long moment and thought about her summer of hard work. Then, because she had a kind heart, she shared some of her food with him anyway.

"Next year, you really must prepare for winter," she said gently but firmly. The grasshopper promised that he would, and he finally learned to work hard and plan ahead.

"Next season, you really must prepare," she said gently but firmly. The grasshopper promised that he would, and he finally learned the value of hard work and planning ahead.

All summer long, the ant worked diligently and without complaint, storing a growing provision of food in her home every single day in careful preparation for the coming winter season.

The grasshopper did not work at all during the warm season, no matter how often the ant gently reminded him. Instead, he spent his days playing music and singing cheerful songs in the sun, never once reflecting seriously on what winter might eventually bring to the unprepared field.

"Why do you work so hard every single day?" he asked one afternoon, settling onto a leaf nearby. "Come and play with me instead of worrying so much about preparation!"

"I am building a provision of food for the long winter season," replied the ant patiently. "You should really be doing the same preparation, before it becomes too late."

The grasshopper only laughed loudly at her warning. "Winter is still so far away," he said carelessly, giving no thought to the consequence of his choice, and he kept playing happily through the whole summer, never once helping with the harvest.

At last, winter finally arrived, and the weather turned bitterly cold almost overnight. Snow covered the entire field, and the grasshopper suddenly faced the full consequence of his careless summer: he had no food left anywhere nearby.

Hungry and cold, he went to the ant's home and knocked weakly on her door. "Please help me," he begged quietly. "I have no food, because I did not prepare when I had the chance."

The ant looked at him for a long moment and thought carefully, reflecting on her whole summer of hard work. Then, moved by genuine generosity, she decided to share some of her provision with him anyway, even though he had mocked her all summer long.

"Next season, you really must prepare ahead of time," she said gently but firmly. The grasshopper promised that he would, and he finally learned, through his own mistake and the ant's generosity, the true value of preparation, careful planning, and second chances.

All summer long, the ant worked diligently and without complaint, methodically storing an ever-growing provision of food in her home every single day in careful preparation for the coming winter season, never once allowing herself a day of rest from this important, necessary task that she had set for herself.

The grasshopper, by contrast, did not work at all during the warm season, no matter how often the ant gently and patiently reminded him of what was eventually coming his way. Instead, he spent his days playing music and singing cheerful songs in the sun, never once reflecting seriously on what winter might eventually bring to the unprepared field around him.

"Why do you work so hard every single day?" he asked one afternoon, settling onto a leaf nearby with a lazy, dismissive grin. "Come and play with me instead of worrying so much about preparation!"

"I am building a provision of food for the long winter season," replied the ant patiently, without looking up from her work. "You should really be doing the same preparation yourself, before it becomes too late to do anything meaningful about it."

The grasshopper only laughed loudly at her repeated warning. "Winter is still so far away," he said carelessly, giving no real thought to the eventual consequence of his choice, and he kept playing happily through the whole summer, never once helping with the harvest or the storing.

At last, winter finally arrived, and the weather turned bitterly cold almost overnight. Snow covered the entire field, and the grasshopper suddenly faced the full consequence of his careless summer: he had no food left anywhere nearby, and nowhere left to turn for help.

Hungry and cold, he went to the ant's home and knocked weakly on her door. "Please help me," he begged quietly, his voice barely audible. "I have no food, because I did not prepare when I had the chance to do so."

The ant looked at him for a long moment and thought carefully, reflecting quietly on her whole summer of hard, uncomplaining work and on everything she had sacrificed to complete it properly and without any help from him. Then, moved by genuine generosity rather than any desire to prove herself right or to gloat over his misfortune, she decided to share some of her hard-earned provision with him anyway, even though he had mocked her relentlessly all summer long for her efforts.

"Next season, you really must prepare ahead of time," she said gently but firmly, placing some food carefully before him. The grasshopper promised that he would, and he finally learned, through his own costly mistake and the ant's unexpected generosity, the true and lasting value of preparation, careful planning, and second chances freely given.

versions.title: The Ant and the Lazy Grasshopper
versions.text:
An ant and a grasshopper lived together in a sunny field at the edge of a quiet farm, where the seasons changed quickly and predictably from warm to cold each year, just as they always had for as long as anyone in the field could remember or had ever bothered to notice; all summer long, the ant worked diligently and without complaint, methodically storing an ever-growing provision of food in her home every single day in careful preparation for the coming winter season, never once allowing herself a day of rest from this important, necessary task that she had long ago set for herself and never questioned.

The grasshopper, by sharp contrast, did not work at all during the warm season, no matter how often the ant gently and patiently reminded him of what was eventually coming his way regardless of his wishes; instead, he spent his days playing music and singing cheerful songs in the sun, never once reflecting seriously on what winter might eventually bring to the unprepared field around him and to him personally, since reflection of that kind had never come naturally to him.

"Why do you work so hard every single day?" he asked one afternoon, settling onto a leaf nearby with a lazy, dismissive grin that irritated the ant more than he realized. "Come and play with me instead of worrying so much about preparation!"

"I am building a provision of food for the long winter season," replied the ant patiently, without even looking up from her steady work. "You should really be doing the same preparation yourself, before it becomes entirely too late to do anything meaningful about it."

The grasshopper only laughed loudly at her repeated warning, as he had laughed at every warning before it. "Winter is still so far away," he said carelessly, giving no real thought whatsoever to the eventual consequence of his choice, and he kept playing happily through the whole summer, never once helping with the harvest or the storing of food.

At last, winter finally arrived, and the weather turned bitterly cold almost overnight, as it always eventually did. Snow covered the entire field, and the grasshopper suddenly faced the full consequence of his careless summer: he had no food left anywhere nearby, and nowhere left to turn for help.

Hungry and cold, he went to the ant's home and knocked weakly on her door. "Please help me," he begged quietly, his voice barely audible through the cold. "I have no food, because I did not prepare when I had the chance to do so."

The ant looked at him for a long moment and thought carefully, reflecting quietly on her whole summer of hard, uncomplaining work and on everything she had sacrificed to complete it properly without any help from him at all. Then, moved by genuine generosity rather than any desire to prove herself right or to gloat over his misfortune, she decided to share some of her hard-earned provision with him anyway, even though he had mocked her relentlessly all summer long for her efforts.

"Next season, you really must prepare ahead of time," she said gently but firmly, placing some food carefully before him as she spoke. The grasshopper promised that he would, and he finally learned, through his own costly mistake and the ant's unexpected generosity, the true and lasting value of preparation, careful planning, and second chances freely given.

keyWords.definition: a small insect that lives and works together with many others
keyWords.example: An ant carried a crumb of bread across the sidewalk.

keyWords.definition: a jumping insect with long back legs that often makes a chirping sound
keyWords.example: A green grasshopper jumped high over the tall grass.

keyWords.definition: the warmest season of the year
keyWords.example: We swam in the lake every day during summer.

keyWords.definition: the coldest season of the year
keyWords.example: Snow covered the whole town in winter.

keyWords.definition: to give part of what you have to someone else
keyWords.example: My friend shared her lunch with me when I forgot mine.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: A grasshopper that quickly moves to a new field to find greener grass to eat
An ant who stores food, and a grasshopper who learns a lesson
A farmer who plants fresh corn every single spring and waits for the rain
Two ants that build a nest together underground, then dig long tunnels
questions.why: The story follows an ant who stores food all summer and a grasshopper who learns an important lesson after refusing to do the same.

wrong.A: The grasshopper stays in the same field the whole story.
wrong.C: No farmer or corn appears in the story.
wrong.D: The story is about one ant and one grasshopper, not two ants.

questions.stem: What problem does the grasshopper face when winter comes?
options: He has too much food saved up
He is attacked by a hungry fox
He loses his way back to the field
He has no food and is hungry and cold
questions.why: When winter arrives, the grasshopper has no food left and is cold and hungry because he did not store any food.

wrong.A: The grasshopper has no food at all, not too much.
wrong.B: No fox appears in the story.
wrong.C: The grasshopper knows exactly where the ant's home is.

questions.stem: What does the ant do every day all summer?
options: She stores food for the winter every day
She sings songs and plays all day
She builds a new home underground
She visits other fields to trade food
questions.why: All through the summer, the ant works hard, storing a little more food every day for winter.

wrong.B: Singing and playing all day describes the grasshopper, not the ant.
wrong.C: The story does not describe the ant building a new home.
wrong.D: The ant does not travel to trade food in the story.

questions.stem: In the story, prepare means —
options: to play and have a lot of fun outside
to sing a song very loudly for others
to get ready for something ahead of time
to argue loudly about who is right
questions.why: The ant tells the grasshopper he must prepare for winter, meaning he must get ready for it ahead of time.

wrong.A: Playing outside describes the grasshopper's summer, not the word prepare.
wrong.B: Singing describes the grasshopper, not the meaning of prepare.
wrong.D: Arguing is not what prepare means in the story.

questions.stem: Why does the ant share her food with the grasshopper?
options: She wants the grasshopper to work for her
She has a kind heart, even though he mocked her
She has too much food and must get rid of it
She wants to win an argument with him
questions.why: Even though the grasshopper laughed at her all summer, the ant's kind heart leads her to share some of her food with him anyway.

wrong.A: The ant shares her food freely; she does not ask for work in return.
wrong.C: The ant stored only what she needed, not extra food to get rid of.
wrong.D: The ant is not trying to win an argument when she shares her food.

questions.stem: What does the grasshopper's laughing at the ant show about him?
options: He does not think ahead about what winter will bring
He is the smartest animal in the whole field, and he knows best
He already has food saved for the winter in his house
He plans to help the ant with her work in the field
questions.why: The grasshopper laughs at the ant's warnings and keeps playing, showing that he is not thinking ahead about winter at all.

wrong.B: Laughing at good advice does not show wisdom.
wrong.C: The grasshopper has no food saved; that is why he needs the ant's help.
wrong.D: The grasshopper never helps the ant with her work.

questions.stem: What happens because the grasshopper does not prepare for winter?
options: The ant loses all of her stored food
Winter never comes to the field at all
The grasshopper quickly finds his own food
The grasshopper has nothing to eat in winter
questions.why: Because the grasshopper spends all summer playing instead of storing food, he has nothing to eat when winter finally arrives.

wrong.A: The ant's food stays safe in her home the whole story.
wrong.B: Winter does arrive in the story, just as the ant warned.
wrong.C: The grasshopper cannot find food; that is why he goes to the ant.

questions.stem: Why does the author show the ant inviting the grasshopper to prepare, and the grasshopper refusing?
options: To show that singing is more useful than working in the summer
To explain how ants build their underground homes
To set up the difference that leads to the story's lesson
To describe what the field looks like in summer
questions.why: This early difference in choices sets up the whole story's lesson about preparation, consequences, and kindness.

wrong.A: Singing does not help the grasshopper survive winter.
wrong.B: The story does not explain how ant homes are built.
wrong.D: Describing the field is not the main point of this exchange.

LOW.prompt: Do you think the ant was right to share her food with the grasshopper? Explain your answer using at least two details from the story.
checklist: I clearly said what I think.
I used at least two details from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: I think the ant was right to share her food with the grasshopper. Even though he laughed at her all summer and did not store any food, she still had a kind heart. She also told him he must prepare next time, which helped him learn an important lesson. Sharing her food was kind, and it also gave him a real chance to do better.

keyWords.definition: to keep something safe so it can be used later
keyWords.example: Squirrels store nuts in the ground before winter.

keyWords.definition: to get ready for something before it happens
keyWords.example: The class prepared for the test by studying every night.

keyWords.definition: the time when ripe crops or food are gathered
keyWords.example: Farmers worked long hours during the harvest.

keyWords.definition: being caring and generous toward other people
keyWords.example: Her kindness toward the new student made him feel welcome.

keyWords.definition: one of the four main parts of the year, such as summer or winter
keyWords.example: Leaves fall from the trees in the autumn season.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the story?
options: A grasshopper and an ant compete in a running race every season
An ant's habit of storing food contrasts sharply with a grasshopper's choices
A kind farmer teaches the field's insects how to harvest crops
Two clever insects build a shared home together for the whole long winter
questions.why: The story contrasts the ant's steady habit of storing food with the grasshopper's carefree choices, leading to the story's lesson about preparation and kindness.

wrong.A: No race takes place in the story.
wrong.C: No farmer teaches harvesting in the story.
wrong.D: The ant and grasshopper do not share a home.

questions.stem: What does the ant do with her food every single day during the summer season?
options: She stores a little more food each day for the winter season
She quietly sells it to the other animals in the field for money
She eats all of it right away without waiting
She shares it with the grasshopper each evening
questions.why: All through the summer, the ant works hard, storing a little more food in her home every single day for the coming winter season.

wrong.B: The ant does not sell food to other animals in the story.
wrong.C: The ant saves her food instead of eating it right away.
wrong.D: The ant does not give away her food until the grasshopper truly needs it.

questions.stem: What does the grasshopper do instead of helping with the harvest?
options: He quietly helps the ant gather and store food
He plants his own separate crop nearby
He asks the farmer for advice about winter
He plays music and sings, never helping at all
questions.why: The grasshopper spends the whole summer playing music and singing cheerful songs, never once helping with the harvest.

wrong.A: The grasshopper never helps the ant store food.
wrong.B: The grasshopper does not plant his own crop in the story.
wrong.C: No farmer appears in this version of the story.

questions.stem: In the story, kindness means —
options: being jealous of what someone else has
being angry about a broken promise
being caring and generous toward others
being afraid of the cold winter season
questions.why: Because of her kindness, the ant shares her food with the grasshopper, meaning she is caring and generous toward him.

wrong.A: Jealousy is not the feeling described as kindness.
wrong.B: Anger is the opposite of the kindness the ant shows.
wrong.D: Fear of winter is not what kindness means in the story.

questions.stem: Why does the ant most likely keep checking on her food supply through the season?
options: She forgets how much food she has stored
She wants to be sure she has enough to last the winter
She plans to trade her food with the grasshopper in the spring
She is bored and has nothing else to do
questions.why: Her careful, steady work suggests she wants to be certain she has stored enough food to prepare fully for the long winter season.

wrong.A: The ant remembers exactly how much food she has stored.
wrong.C: The ant does not plan to trade food with the grasshopper.
wrong.D: Her careful work shows purpose, not boredom.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the grasshopper's attitude toward the harvest season?
options: He does not take the harvest season seriously at all
He works harder than the ant during harvest
He secretly stores food without telling anyone in his home
He helps every animal in the field prepare
questions.why: By playing and singing instead of helping with the harvest, the grasshopper shows that he does not take the season's importance seriously.

wrong.B: The grasshopper does far less work than the ant.
wrong.C: The grasshopper stores no food at all, secretly or otherwise.
wrong.D: The grasshopper does not help anyone prepare.

questions.stem: Why does the winter season hit the grasshopper so hard?
options: Because the ant refuses to open her door
Because the season changes earlier than usual
Because the field runs out of room for insects
Because he never stored or prepared any food
questions.why: Winter is especially hard on the grasshopper because he never stored or prepared any food during the warm season.

wrong.A: The ant does open her door and helps him.
wrong.B: The story does not say winter arrives earlier than usual.
wrong.C: Running out of room is not mentioned in the story.

questions.stem: How does the author organize the events of the story?
options: By comparing two separate harvest festivals in the town
By showing summer choices, then their winter results
By listing facts about insects in general and their homes
By telling the ending before the beginning of the tale
questions.why: The story first shows each character's choices during the summer season, then shows the results of those choices once winter arrives.

wrong.A: No harvest festivals are compared in the story.
wrong.C: The story is a narrative, not a list of facts.
wrong.D: The events are told in order, from summer to winter.

MID.prompt: Explain how the ant's preparation and the grasshopper's lack of preparation led to very different winters for each of them. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how each character's choices affected their winter.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: The ant's preparation and the grasshopper's lack of preparation led to very different winters. All summer, the ant stored a little more food every day, so when winter came, she had plenty to eat. The grasshopper, by contrast, spent the whole season playing and never helped with the harvest, so he had no food once winter arrived. Because of his choices, the grasshopper ended up cold and hungry, while the ant's steady preparation kept her safe and fed.

keyWords.definition: the act of getting ready for something before it happens
keyWords.example: Careful preparation helped the team win the championship.

keyWords.definition: a result or effect that follows from an earlier action or choice
keyWords.example: Forgetting his umbrella was a direct consequence of ignoring the forecast.

keyWords.definition: the quality of giving freely and caring about other people's needs
keyWords.example: The family's generosity provided meals for the whole shelter.

keyWords.definition: a stored supply of something, especially food, kept for future use
keyWords.example: The ship carried enough provisions to last the entire voyage.

keyWords.definition: to think carefully and seriously about something
keyWords.example: Before answering, the scientist paused to reflect on the data.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the story?
options: A grasshopper and an ant permanently end their friendship
A farmer rewards the hardest-working insect in the field
Poor preparation has consequences, but generosity allows a second chance
Two insects permanently abandon the field after a harsh, bitter winter
questions.why: The story shows that a lack of preparation leads to real consequences for the grasshopper, while the ant's generosity still offers him a second chance.

wrong.A: The ant ultimately helps the grasshopper rather than ending their relationship.
wrong.B: No farmer appears in the story.
wrong.D: Neither insect abandons the field in the story.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe the grasshopper mocking the ant before winter arrives?
options: To prove that singing is a more valuable skill than storing food
To explain the biology of how insects survive the cold
To criticize the ant for working harder than necessary
To set up the consequence the grasshopper will soon face
questions.why: Showing the grasshopper's mockery before winter sets up the consequence he faces once his lack of preparation catches up with him.

wrong.A: Singing provides no food, which winter soon makes clear.
wrong.B: The story does not explain insect biology.
wrong.C: The ant's hard work is never criticized in the story.

questions.stem: What ultimately leads to the ant's decision to share her provision with the grasshopper?
options: A promise she made to the grasshopper earlier in summer in the field
Reflecting on her own hard work and feeling genuine generosity
A rule that all insects in the field must follow
Advice given by a wise old insect living nearby
questions.why: After reflecting carefully on her own summer of work, the ant is moved by genuine generosity to share her provision with the grasshopper.

wrong.A: The ant made no such promise earlier in the story.
wrong.C: No rule requires the insects to share food.
wrong.D: No wise old insect gives advice in the story.

questions.stem: In the story, the word provision most nearly means —
options: a stored supply of something, especially food
a type of insect that lives underground
a rule that every animal in the field follows
a type of plant that grows in winter
questions.why: The ant's provision is the supply of food she carefully stored throughout the summer for use later in winter.

wrong.B: Provision does not refer to an insect in the story.
wrong.C: No field-wide rule is called a provision.
wrong.D: Provision does not name a type of plant in the story.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the grasshopper's lack of reflection during the summer?
options: He secretly planned for winter the whole time
He understood the consequences before they arrived
He did not consider what his choices would eventually cost him
He secretly wanted the ant to fail right along with him in the cold
questions.why: Because the grasshopper never seriously reflects on winter while he mocks the ant, he fails to consider what his careless choices will eventually cost him.

wrong.A: The grasshopper makes no winter plans at all.
wrong.B: He clearly does not understand the consequences until they arrive.
wrong.D: The story gives no sign that he wishes failure on the ant.

questions.stem: How does the grasshopper's attitude toward preparation compare with the ant's?
options: The ant values preparation, while the grasshopper dismisses it entirely
Both insects equally value careful preparation all season long
The grasshopper actually prepares more carefully than the ant does
Neither insect ever thinks preparation matters at all, they say
questions.why: The ant consistently values preparation throughout the summer, while the grasshopper dismisses her warnings and does nothing to prepare.

wrong.B: The grasshopper shows no interest in preparation at all.
wrong.C: The ant, not the grasshopper, is the one who prepares carefully.
wrong.D: The ant clearly believes preparation matters a great deal.

questions.stem: What is the direct consequence of the grasshopper's lack of preparation?
options: The ant loses her entire stored provision
The field experiences an early, unexpected harvest
The grasshopper quickly finds another food source
The grasshopper faces real hunger once winter arrives
questions.why: Because the grasshopper never prepared any provision of his own, he faces real, immediate hunger once winter finally arrives.

wrong.A: The ant's provision remains safe throughout the story.
wrong.B: No early or unexpected harvest is mentioned.
wrong.C: The grasshopper finds no food on his own; that is why he seeks the ant's help.

questions.stem: What does the ant's generosity ultimately suggest about offering someone a second chance?
options: Second chances should basically never be given to anyone who has made a mistake
Generosity can give someone a real chance to reflect and improve
Preparation matters more than generosity
Consequences should be avoided whatever happens
questions.why: The ant's generosity gives the grasshopper the chance to reflect on his mistake and genuinely improve, suggesting that kindness can open the door to real change.

wrong.A: The ant's choice to help shows the opposite: she does offer a second chance.
wrong.C: The story values both preparation and generosity, not one over the other.
wrong.D: The grasshopper faces real consequences; they are not avoided.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says someone who refuses to prepare for the future does not deserve help later on. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about the ant and the grasshopper.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I disagree that someone who refuses to prepare for the future does not deserve help later on. The grasshopper ignored every warning and mocked the ant's hard work all summer, yet the ant still chose generosity over resentment when winter came. Her kindness did not erase the real consequence he faced, since he still went hungry and cold until she helped him, but it gave him a genuine chance to reflect and change. Someone might argue that helping him removes any reason to prepare next time, but the story shows the opposite: the experience, combined with the ant's generosity, is exactly what finally teaches him the lasting value of preparation.

LOW.stem: What does the grasshopper do all day in the sun?
options: He plays and sings.
He stores some food.
He digs a deep hole.
He builds a warm home.
LOW.why: In the text, he played all day and sang in the sun.

wrong.B: The ant stores the food, not the grasshopper.
wrong.C: Digging a hole is not mentioned.
wrong.D: Building a home is not mentioned.

LOW.stem: In the story, the word store means —
options: to throw it far away
to eat it very fast
to keep it for later
to sing it very loudly
LOW.why: The ant stores food all summer so she will have it for winter.

wrong.A: She keeps the food; she does not throw it away.
wrong.B: She saves the food for winter and does not eat it at once.
wrong.D: Storing food is not about singing.

LOW.stem: Why does the grasshopper go to the ant's home?
options: He wants to play again.
He lost his song book.
He wants to see snow.
He is cold and hungry.
LOW.why: Winter comes, he has no food, and he is cold and hungry, so he asks the ant for help.

wrong.A: He is asking for help, not for play.
wrong.B: A song book is not mentioned.
wrong.C: Snow is already falling.

LOW.stem: What does the ant's last sentence tell us about her?
options: She is angry and very cruel.
She is kind but wants change.
She wants to be left alone.
She has forgotten the summer.
LOW.why: She shares her food but also says he must prepare next year, so she is kind but wants him to change.

wrong.A: She shares her food, so she is not cruel.
wrong.C: She talks with him and helps him.
wrong.D: She remembers, which is why she tells him to prepare.

MID.stem: How does the ant sound when she tells the grasshopper to prepare next season?
options: Loud and angry
Sad and tearful
Silly and playful
Gentle but firm
MID.why: The text says she spoke gently but firmly.

wrong.A: She does not shout.
wrong.B: She is not described as crying.
wrong.C: She is serious about the warning.

MID.stem: In the story, the word bitterly in "bitterly cold" means —
options: extremely
slightly
sometimes
never
MID.why: Snow covers the field, so the cold is extreme.

wrong.B: Snow means the cold is more than slight.
wrong.C: The cold is described as a present condition, not an occasional one.
wrong.D: The weather is cold, so never does not fit.

MID.stem: What does the ant's long pause before sharing suggest?
options: She has forgotten his name.
She cannot hear him knock.
She is deciding what to do.
She is too sleepy to talk.
MID.why: She looks at him for a long moment and thinks about her summer of hard work before she shares.

wrong.A: She knows who he is.
wrong.B: She opens the door and looks at him.
wrong.D: Sleepiness is not mentioned.

MID.stem: What does the grasshopper learn because of his hungry winter?
options: That songs bring free food.
That planning ahead matters.
That winter is a short time.
That the ant is not kind.
MID.why: The text says he learned the value of hard work and planning ahead.

wrong.A: His songs did not bring him food.
wrong.C: He learns winter is hard, not short.
wrong.D: The ant is kind and shares her food.

HIGH.stem: How does winter arrive in the field?
options: Slowly, with a warm breeze
Only after a long, mild fall
Almost overnight, and very cold
With a loud storm of rain
HIGH.why: The text says the weather turned bitterly cold almost overnight.

wrong.A: The weather turns bitterly cold, not warm.
wrong.B: The change is sudden, not slow.
wrong.D: Snow covers the field, not rain.

HIGH.stem: In the story, the word diligently most nearly means —
options: with a loud complaint
with a lazy, tired smile
with a sudden, silly joke
with steady, careful effort
HIGH.why: The ant worked diligently all summer, storing food every single day without complaint.

wrong.A: The ant worked without complaint.
wrong.B: The ant was hard-working, not lazy.
wrong.C: The ant was serious about her work.

HIGH.stem: Why does the author say the seasons changed "quickly and predictably"?
options: To show winter is no surprise
To explain why ants are small
To say the farm is far away
To describe the grasshopper's song
HIGH.why: If winter comes on time every year, the grasshopper should have been ready for it.

wrong.B: The size of ants is not the point.
wrong.C: The detail is about seasons, not distance.
wrong.D: The sentence is about seasons, not his song.

HIGH.stem: Why might sharing her provision have been hard for the ant?
options: She had nothing left to eat.
He had mocked her all summer.
He was not hungry enough.
Her home was too far away.
HIGH.why: The text says she shared even though he had mocked her all summer long.

wrong.A: She has enough food to share.
wrong.C: He is hungry and cold.
wrong.D: He goes to her home and knocks on her door.
